Read out of saint.gr's line for 22 Ιουνίου, «Άγιος Ευσέβιος», with the rank word left off. The day's line carries no see; the life page behind it calls him «επίσκοπος Σαμοσάτων».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 22. јун ст. ст., „Свештеномученик Јевсевије, епископ самосатски“ — Свештеномученик is the rank and „епископ самосатски“ is a second rank and the see, and §6 takes both off, as this folder’s Romanian note already says in its own words. The bare forename is what is left. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Јевсевије», **which is the most surprising measurement of the day**: the corpus keeps a dozen Eusebius folders and this is the first `sr` form of the name on any of them, so a name that looks like a certain fold is not one. Measured, not suspected.
Read out of the name link behind his place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 22 июня ст. ст., «Евсевий Самосатский, сщмч.», with the grade word left off.

death.note: Two books, two years one apart, and the field is widened rather than chosen. doxologia’s life, as this folder’s own life has it: «One day in the year 380», when he was struck on the head and died. The Охридски пролог for 22. јун ст. ст. ends the entry „Пострада 379. године“ — he suffered in the year 379. One year is not close enough to choose on; nothing is averaged and neither book is preferred. The three books also disagree about the thrower, the missile and the place of the blow, which is written in the life and in no field (5 October 2026).

feast.note: The same menologion number this folder's three other venerated rows carry. His life page life1375 heads «День памяти: 22 июня» and names no other day; it was read whole and its account agrees with what this folder already carries — Nicaea, the act of the council for Meletius of Antioch, the two hands held out to Constantius, Julian, the Arian sent to Samosata, Gratian's recall, the roof-tile at Doliche, the forgiving of the woman and the nephew who followed him — so no paragraph was added and the kontakion is what this upgrade brings. That page dates his death about 380, inside the interval this folder already records.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries. The day's line gives only «Άγιος Ευσέβιος», but the page names him bishop of Samosata, so against the corpus's eight other men of the name it is this one: exiled under Valens to a desert place by the river Ister and killed by a stone thrown at his head by a heretic woman. The page's heading reads «(; - 380)» and its narrative puts the blow in «το έτος 380 μ.Χ.», a year the folder carries no `dates` for; the year is reported rather than written, because the folder's own source gives none. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 05.07.2026 (22. јун ст. ст.) — „Свештеномученик Јевсевије, епископ самосатски“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 22 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **THE DATE IS WIDENED BY ONE YEAR, WHICH IS THE NARROWEST WIDENING OF THIS WAVE AND IS STILL A WIDENING.** The folder held `death` 380 to 380, display «380», off doxologia’s «One day in the year 380» — the sentence saint.gr also carries, and the folder’s note cites it as doxologia’s. This book ends the entry „Пострада 379. године“ — he suffered in the year 379. `death` earliest 379, latest 380, display «379 or 380», basis traditional, both sentences in the note. The «X or Y» form and not the dash, neither side being a stated range. **One year is not close enough to choose on**: nothing is averaged and no book is preferred, and the rule does not have a threshold below which a disagreement stops counting. **AND THE THREE BOOKS DISAGREE ABOUT THE DEATH ITSELF, IN A WAY THAT PUTS THIS ONE WITH THE ROMANIAN AND AGAINST THE GREEK.** doxologia has him enter Doliche with the bishop he had just consecrated, and an Arian **woman** throw a brick down **from a roof** onto his head. saint.gr has him, back in his see and cleaning his province, pass **outside the house** of a heretic woman who strikes him on the head with a **great stone**. This book: he came to Doliche with the chosen bishop to enthrone him and to refute the Arian heresy, which was strong in that city, and „неки фанатички јеретик баци с крова ћерамиду на Јевсевијеву главу“ — **some fanatical heretic** threw a **roof tile** from a roof onto his head. So it agrees with doxologia on the city, the errand, the roof and the tile, and differs from it on the thrower, who is a man here and a woman there; and it differs from saint.gr on all of it. All three are written and none is chosen. **The forgiveness is doxologia’s alone** — the oath Eusebius put on his companions to take no revenge on the woman — and it is left standing in the folder’s older prose untouched, this book having a male thrower and no oath. **THE EPISODE NO OTHER BOOK HAS, AND IT IS THE BEST THING ON THE DAY.** Under Julian the Apostate, „свети Јевсевије скиде са себе свештеничке расе а обуче се у војничко одело, те под видом војника обилазаше гоњене цркве по Сирији, Финикији и Палестини“ — he put off his priestly robes and put on a soldier’s dress, and under the appearance of a soldier went round the persecuted churches through Syria, Phoenicia and Palestine, everywhere strengthening the orthodox faith and appointing the needed priests and deacons and other clergy, and in places even bishops. **Neither other book has one word of it.** saint.gr had only that new and heavier troubles began for him under Julian and that he stayed unshaken; doxologia passes from the Arians to Valens. **AND IT DOES NOT MAKE HIM A `soldier`.** The disguise is in the body, the heading gives Свештеномученик and епископ and nothing else, and a man in a soldier’s coat is not a soldier even in a body. `types` UNTOUCHED: `hieromartyr` and `bishop` are both there, and the `office` «Bishop» is already set. THE COUNCIL, AND WHY ITS YEAR IS IN NO FIELD. „свети Јевсевије усаветова Мелетија те сазва сабор у Антиохији 361. године“, a council of twenty-seven hierarchs which condemned the Arian heresy again and proclaimed the faith as the first universal council had expressed it. **A Council is not a folder** and a council’s year is not a person’s date, so 361 is written nowhere; and the number of hierarchs is a count. The entry also says the Council was „у време благочестивог цара Јовиниана“, in the time of the pious emperor Jovian — **which does not sit with its own 361**, Jovian reigning after Julian, whose death the same sentence places before the council. The two statements are this book’s own and they are left as they are: a reader does not repair a source, and nothing is derived from either of them because neither is a date of this man. THE EXILES AND THE RESTORATIONS, WHICH THIS BOOK NAMES MORE EXACTLY THAN EITHER OTHER. Under Valens: Meletius to Armenia, Eusebius to **Thrace**, Pelagius to Arabia — where saint.gr had a desert place near the river Ister and doxologia named no destination at all. Under Gratian the three return, Meletius to Antioch, Eusebius to Samosata, Pelagius to Laodicea, **which is doxologia’s sentence exactly**, so two books now agree on it. **ROWS: ONE STANDS, THREE ARE REFUSED.** `meletius-of-antioch` is `related` on this folder and on that one in both directions already, is named in the folder’s older prose, and this book’s whole first half is about the two of them — the row stands untouched and the name may stay in the prose. **`john-chrysostom` takes no row and no mention in the prose**: this book says Meletius „се по смрти удостојио велике похвале од стране светог Јована Златоуста“, which is a praise of **Meletius** and not of this man, so it is not his story; and `eusebius-of-samosata` holds no row to Chrysostom in either direction, where `meletius-of-antioch` does. **Pelagius of Laodicea takes no row**: `ls saints | grep -i pelagi` returns `pelagius-of-lefkada` alone, who is of Lefkada and not of Laodicea, so the famed virgin and ascetic of this entry has no folder — and **no `virgin` type is written anywhere off him either**, there being nothing to write it on. **Marinus takes no row**: `ls saints | grep -i marinus` returns five and not one of them is a bishop of Doliche, and an identification off a name in another man’s life is not an identification. `constantine-the-great` is `related` already, this book naming Constantius as his evil son, and is untouched. The emperors — Constantius, Julian the Apostate, Jovian, Valens, Gratian — take no rows and are no source for a year. No `locations`: Samosata, Antioch, Syria, Phoenicia, Palestine, Thrace, Armenia, Arabia, Laodicea and Doliche are ten places in one entry and every one of them is named in a clause. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE VERSE IS NOT USED. The ПЕСМА for 22 June is about the first entry and names its three men as three stars — „Јевсевије, и с њим Мелетије, Ко две звезде – трећа: Пелагије“ — and it opens „Црква никад није без пастира“, the Church is never without a shepherd. It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not the entry’s account, so §3 of this wave’s brief puts it in no field and in no life, and it is recorded here instead. **NOTHING IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER ON THIS DAY, WHICH HAS NOT HAPPENED BEFORE IN THIS WAVE.** The Prologue prints two entries for the Julian 22 June and the corpus holds every person in both headings: `eusebius-of-samosata` off two calendars, `zeno-the-martyr-22-june` and `zenas-the-martyr-22-june` off two more. Nineteen days before this one produced sixty-seven upgrades and no new folder, and four days in five refused somebody; this is the fifth day. It is worth recording as the shape of a day rather than as an absence: the corpus holds nine folders on the menologion 22/6 and this book names three of them and nobody else.

hymns.text: Şi părtaş obiceiurilor şi următor scaunelor apostolilor fiind, lucrare ai aflat, de Dumnezeu insuflate, spre suirea privirii la cele înalte. Pentru aceasta, cuvântul adevărului drept învăţând şi cu credinţa răbdând până la sânge Sfinţite Mucenice Eusebiu, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Sfințit Mucenic Eusebiu, Episcopul Samosatelor, glasul 4; the text is the common of a hieromartyr, printed with his name in it.

english.text: Having become a sharer of the apostles' ways and a successor to their thrones, thou didst find in action, O God-inspired one, an ascent to contemplation. Therefore, rightly dividing the word of truth, and contending for the faith even unto blood, O Hieromartyr Eusebius, intercede with Christ God that our souls be saved.

hymns.text: Σοφίας τοῦ Πνεύματος, καταυγασθεῖς τῷ φωτί, τὸν λόγον ἐτράνωσας, τῆς εὐσέβειας ἠμίν, Εὐσέβιε ἔνδοξε, σὺ γὰρ ἱεραρχήσας, εὐσεβῶς τὴ Τριάδι, ἤθλησας θεοφρόνως, καὶ τὴν πλάνην καθεῖλες. Καὶ νῦν Πάτερ δυσώπησον, σώζεσθαι ἅπαντας.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the first of two apolytikia on the page of «Άγιος Ευσέβιος», and it names him; the second is the common of a hierarch, «Κανόνα πίστεως», and is not taken

english.text: Lit up by the light of the Spirit's wisdom, you made plain to us the word of piety, O glorious Eusebius; for having served as a hierarch piously before the Trinity, you contended with a godly mind and brought down error. And now, father, entreat that all may be saved.

hymns.text: Благочестно во святительстве пожив/ и мучения путь прошед,/ идольския угасил еси жертвы, святителю Евсевие,/ но яко имеяй дерзновение ко Христу Богу,// моли спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 22 июня ст. ст. — «Кондак священномученика Евсевия», глас 4. Proper to him — «святителю Евсевие» in the vocative — and the only hymn this day page prints for anybody.

english.text: Having lived in piety in the hierarchy and passed through the way of martyrdom, thou didst quench the sacrifices of the idols, hierarch Eusebius; and having boldness before Christ God, pray that our souls may be saved.
